common_name: Rosemond Coles Canna (Heirloom Fiery Red Flowers Edged Gold)

planting.note: Plant divided rhizomes once soil has warmed past 60°F; Rosemond Coles is a long-grown heirloom bearing fiery red petals broadly margined in golden yellow over plain green foliage, a bicolor combination distinct from the solid-colored or spotted heirloom cannas.

directions: Set rhizomes 3-4 inches deep in rich, moisture-retentive soil in full sun, and feed monthly through the growing season to keep the vigorous clumps blooming from midsummer into fall. Rosemond Coles holds its broad gold edge consistently across the bloom season, which has kept it in commerce as a standard heirloom bedding canna for decades even as newer striped- and dark-foliage selections have become fashionable. Keep soil evenly moist but well drained, since cannas are heavy feeders and drinkers that rot quickly in standing water. In zone 9 and warmer it overwinters in the ground and expands into a full clump; farther north, lift and store rhizomes after the first frost blackens the foliage.
sources: Iowa State University Extension and Outreach — Recommended Canna Cultivars

common_name: King Midas Canna (Heirloom Fawn-Spotted Yellow Canna)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes once soil has warmed; King Midas is a long-cultivated heirloom with large, broad-petaled yellow flowers lightly flecked with fawn-orange spotting over plain green foliage, blooming late into the season.

directions: Plant rhizomes 3-4 inches deep in fertile, consistently moist soil in full sun, and feed monthly to sustain the large late-season flower heads. King Midas has held an RHS Award of Garden Merit on the strength of its clean green foliage and reliably large, softly speckled yellow blooms, which open later in the summer than many heirloom cannas and extend the garden's gold color into early fall. Keep the soil well drained despite regular watering, since cannas rot readily where water stands around the rhizome. In zone 9 and warmer it overwinters in the ground; elsewhere, lift and store rhizomes after the first killing frost.

common_name: Austria Canna (Heirloom Orchid-Flowered Italian-Group Yellow Canna)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes once soil has warmed; Austria is a 19th-century Italian-Group (orchid-flowered) heirloom with large, wide-petaled, self-colored yellow flowers marked with orange-red spotting in the throat, over tall plain green foliage.

directions: Plant rhizomes 3-4 inches deep in rich, moisture-retentive soil in full sun, staking tall stems in exposed sites. Austria was introduced in 1893 by Sprenger's Italian breeding program and belongs to the orchid-flowered group prized for broad, overlapping petals that resemble Cattleya blooms rather than the narrower-petaled flowers of older French and Crozy-type cannas. It is a tall, back-of-border heirloom that pairs well with bronze- or burgundy-leaf cultivars for contrast. In zone 9 and warmer it overwinters in the ground and clumps expand yearly; elsewhere, lift and store rhizomes after frost blackens the foliage.

common_name: Aida Canna (Heirloom Grand Opera Series Soft Pink Canna)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes once soil has warmed; Aida dates to the 1920s Grand Opera canna series and carries soft rose-pink flowers over compact, dark green foliage, smaller in stature than most heirloom cannas.

directions: Set rhizomes 3-4 inches deep in fertile, evenly moist soil in full sun, feeding monthly to keep the compact plants blooming steadily through summer. Aida has stayed in cultivation since its introduction in the Grand Opera canna series nearly a century ago, valued for its clean dark green leaves and gentle rose-pink flower color, which reads softer than the hot reds and oranges typical of the group. Its shorter stature suits mid-border plantings or large containers better than taller heirloom cannas. In zone 9 and warmer it overwinters in the ground; farther north, lift and store rhizomes once frost blackens the foliage.
sources: Iowa State University Extension and Outreach — Recommended Canna Cultivars

common_name: Crimson Beauty Canna (Classic Dark Red-Flowered Green Foliage Canna)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes once soil has warmed; Crimson Beauty bears large, reflexed dark red flowers with pink highlights over broad plain green foliage, a standard-type canna often used as a benchmark for comparing other red cultivars.

directions: Plant rhizomes 3-4 inches deep in rich, consistently moist soil in full sun, feeding monthly from midsummer through fall to sustain its long bloom run. Crimson Beauty has long been treated as the standard medium-height red canna against which newer dark-leaf or striped-foliage red cultivars are measured, prized for clean green leaves that let the deep red, reflexed flowers stand out on their own. It tolerates a wide range of soils provided drainage is adequate, since cannas rot in waterlogged ground. In zone 9 and warmer it overwinters in the ground and forms expanding clumps; elsewhere, lift and store rhizomes after the first frost.
sources: Iowa State University Extension and Outreach — Recommended Canna Cultivars

common_name: Miss Oklahoma Canna (Large-Flowered True Pink Green Foliage Canna)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes once soil has warmed; Miss Oklahoma produces unusually large, broad-petaled watermelon-pink flower heads over wide green foliage, a true pink rarely seen among canna cultivars.

directions: Set rhizomes 3-4 inches deep in rich, moisture-retentive soil in full sun, and feed monthly to support its oversized bloom heads. Miss Oklahoma is grown chiefly for a true, clear pink flower color that stands apart from the salmon, rose, and coral tones common in other canna cultivars, carried on broad green-leafed plants with a strong, self-cleaning habit. It performs well in borders and large containers alike where its bold color and bloom size can be appreciated up close. In zone 9 and warmer it overwinters in the ground; farther north, lift and store rhizomes once frost blackens the foliage.
sources: Iowa State University Extension and Outreach — Recommended Canna Cultivars

common_name: Red Futurity Canna (Dwarf Burgundy-Tinged Foliage Scarlet Canna)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes once soil has warmed; Red Futurity is part of the compact Futurity dwarf canna series, carrying scarlet-red flowers over green foliage tinged with burgundy, well suited to containers and small beds.

directions: Plant rhizomes a few inches deep in fertile, evenly moist soil in full sun, and deadhead spent spikes to encourage continued bloom from summer into frost. Red Futurity belongs to the Futurity dwarf canna series bred for a shorter, bushier habit than standard heirloom cannas, making it a practical choice for the front of a border, poolside planting, or large container where taller cultivars would be out of scale. Feed monthly, since cannas are heavy feeders even in compact forms, and keep soil well drained to avoid rhizome rot. In zone 9 and warmer it overwinters in the ground; elsewhere, lift and store rhizomes after the first frost.

common_name: Striped Beauty Canna (Old White-Pinstriped Foliage Butter-Yellow Canna)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes once soil has warmed; Striped Beauty, also sold as 'Nirvana' or 'Bangkok Yellow', has green leaves finely pinstriped in silvery white and butter-yellow flowers marked with a white central stripe on each petal, distinct from the bolder yellow-and-green Bengal Tiger type.

directions: Plant rhizomes 3-4 inches deep in rich, consistently moist soil in full sun, where strong light brings out the finest white pinstriping in the foliage. Striped Beauty is an old hybrid grown under several trade names, valued for a subtler variegation pattern than the broad yellow-green bands of Bengal Tiger, paired with red flower buds that open to soft butter-yellow blooms striped white down the petal center. It multiplies vigorously into a substantial clump over a season. In zone 9 and warmer it overwinters in the ground; farther north, lift and store rhizomes after the first frost blackens the foliage.

common_name: Pfitzer's Primrose Yellow Canna (Compact Dwarf Pale-Yellow Canna)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes once soil has warmed; Pfitzer's Primrose Yellow is a compact dwarf canna from the Pfitzer breeding line, bearing clusters of pale canary-yellow flowers over plain green foliage on a tidy, well-proportioned plant.

directions: Set rhizomes a few inches deep in fertile, evenly moist soil in full sun, and divide congested clumps every few years to maintain vigor. Pfitzer's Primrose Yellow was bred as part of a dwarf canna line selected for compact, in-proportion growth, making it suitable for smaller garden beds and containers where full-size heirloom cannas would overwhelm the space. Its soft canary-yellow flower clusters are produced freely through the season on a vigorous, well-branched plant. In zone 9 and warmer it overwinters in the ground; elsewhere, lift and store rhizomes after the first killing frost.
sources: Holland Bulb Farms — Pfitzer's Primrose Yellow Dwarf Canna
